units.title: Scheduled maintenance: payroll portal
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: System notice. Ref GLS-SYS-0419. The payroll portal will be unavailable for scheduled maintenance from 22:00 tonight until 02:00 tomorrow (Sound Time). Timesheets submitted during this window will be queued and processed when the service resumes. Statements may arrive up to one hour later than usual. No action is required. This mailbox is not monitored; please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Day-rate accrual statement KH-01
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Statement type: daily accrual. Site: KH-01 (Kittering Holm). Period: 3 of 5. Day rate: $300.00 per active worker, as recorded on the site roster at 21:00 yesterday. Piece rate: $100.00 per tree, per contract schedule C. Accruals are provisional until the period closes. Discrepancies should be raised with Operations, not with this address. Statement reference: KH01-P3-D18.

units.title: Reminder: outstanding crew wages
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Arrears reminder. Site: KH-01. Our records show crew wages outstanding on this site account as at 21:00 yesterday. Under the site lead agreement, crew wages are settled before discretionary purchases. Operations has been copied on this notice. If payment has already been made, please disregard. Reference: KH01-ARR-19. Do not reply to this address.

units.title: Cold snap? We've got you covered!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Brr! The Met Office says a cold, still spell is on its way, and we say: be ready! Five ways to keep your camp cosy: 1. Insulate your water lines. 2. Keep a spare gas canister indoors. 3. Swap to winter-grade fuel. 4. Double up socks (wool, always!). 5. Hang a lantern by every door. All this week, 15% off our Thermal Range. Stay warm out there! The Camp Supply team

units.title: Week three check-in
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a quick round-up for the start of week three: - Supply boat stays on its usual run; the skipper now leaves Gilliver an hour earlier so he is back across before dark. - Fuel order for the next drop is confirmed. - Head office would like numbers by Friday, as usual. - The mainland power cuts are not affecting the depot. Just checking where we are on numbers when you get a moment. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Sorry, one more: the Sound Lines night crossings are still cut back for their review. That is their passenger service, not our boat, so nothing changes for you. I mention it only because some of the crew's families may have read about it and assumed the supply run is affected. It is not. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Press enquiries (again)
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I'm aware the Courier reporter has written to a few people connected with the job. I'd be grateful if any questions continue to come through me. This isn't about hiding anything; it's an ordinary clearance, just a big one, and head office prefers one voice on it. If anyone on the crew is contacted directly, the same applies. I'd rather we didn't make the paper's job easier by accident. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Crew replacement
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, an update on finding someone for the empty place on the crew. I've rung round the usual agencies and two contractors in Tollinby. Nobody can start before next week, and one asked straight out about the stories in the paper, which didn't help. The leaver's paperwork is with payroll. I'll keep trying, but please plan the next few days on the crew you have. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Numbers
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, head office has seen the count go past half the island and asked me to pass on that they are pleased. I said I'd tell you, so I am. They also asked whether the pace holds now the days are shorter. I said yes. If that turns out to be optimistic, I'd rather hear it from you before Friday than from the spreadsheet. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Numbers
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, head office asked me this morning where we are against the halfway mark. I told them the numbers come from site and that I'd have them by Friday. If anything is slowing you down, the yard, the saws, the weather, please tell me plainly and I'll take it upstairs. I'd much rather argue for more kit now than explain a shortfall later. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Generator service sheet
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the hire firm has asked for the hours reading from the camp generator for their service log. No rush, the next drop is fine. If the hour meter reads oddly, a photo is enough. They mentioned their other units on the mainland have been working hard with the power cuts and they are short of engineers, so please keep it fuelled and don't let it run dry. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Re: the thing I said
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. About the Corran thing. Don't put it in an email to Ruth, all right? I mean it. Ask me in a pub when you're back and I'll tell you what I know, which is less than you'd think. Anyway. The road job's gone solid with frost so we're sat in the van doing crosswords. Seven letters, 'one who clears'. I said 'Grieve'. Nobody laughed.

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Also, before I forget: keep your lot together after dark. Not for any reason. It's just what a good site lead does, and you're a good site lead, and that's the nicest thing I'll say all year so don't frame it. Right. Might be off the radar for a bit, the van's got no signal out here. Hal

units.title: No need to reply
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello again. I realise it may not be possible, or wise, for you to reply to me, and I understand completely. I have put the same questions to Grieve and to Ardent Vale. If you ever do want to talk, I can keep your name and role out of anything I write. In the meantime I will only say that people in Gilliver ask after the crew, kindly. Best wishes, Nell Ashdown, The Ammet Courier

units.title: mum update
units.author: sam
units.text: hi, so Mum is out of theatre and sitting up and she's already complaining about the custard, which the nurse said is a very good sign. the surgeon says the new hip went in fine and she'll be on a frame for a bit. she asked if you'd rung and I said you can't really, and she said 'well tell them I'm not dead then'. so. consider yourself told. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: anyway the dress rehearsal is Thursday and the costume is held together with safety pins and hope. the dog has learned to open the kitchen bin with his nose. also the Courier has a thing today about people in Gilliver seeing lights on your island every night. I assume that's you lot. is it really fine out there? you'd say if it wasn't. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: ps our power went off about ten minutes ago, the whole street. I'm writing this on my phone by the light of the oven clock, which is battery, which I didn't know. the kid thinks it's brilliant and wants to sleep in the hall with a torch. the dog is under the table. it's fine. it's just a bit dark here. x

units.title: Sorry, me again
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, I'm sorry to write again. I know you're busy and this isn't your job. Could you tell Tomas I'm fine? We had a power cut on our side of Weyhaven on Sunday night and I sat with my neighbour and her cat and we were perfectly all right. I only mention it in case he hears about it and worries. Is he sleeping? Thank you, Ana

units.title: Your policy documents are ready
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Dear Policyholder, your updated policy schedule (ref LM-VH-20831) is now available in your online account. Please check that your details, including your usual address and the main use of your vehicle, are correct. Inaccurate information may affect a claim. At Lyle Mutual, peace of mind comes as standard. This is an automated message. Terms and conditions apply.

units.title: Timesheet received KH-01
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Your timesheet for site KH-01, day 19, has been received and queued for processing. Note: this timesheet was held during scheduled maintenance and processed at 02:04. Hours and piece counts have been recorded against period 3. A revised accrual will follow in the next scheduled statement. Reference: KH01-TS-D19. This is an automated message from Grieve Payroll.

units.title: Maintenance complete
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: System notice. Ref GLS-SYS-0419-C. Scheduled maintenance on the payroll portal completed at 02:01 Sound Time, one minute later than planned. All queued items have been processed. If you received a duplicate statement for the same period, keep the later one and delete the earlier. We apologise for any inconvenience. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Leaver processed
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Leaver processed. Site: KH-01. A crew member has been removed from the active site roster and a final statement has been issued to their registered address. Day rates for this worker will no longer accrue. Any equipment on loan should be recorded on the site return sheet. Operations has been notified. Reference: KH01-LV-20. Do not reply.

units.title: Is your vehicle winter-ready?
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Cold mornings are here! Before you set off, clear every window, not just a peephole, and check your tyres. Did you know frost-related claims rise by a third in a cold spell? Lyle Mutual Winter Assist can be added to your policy from just a few dollars a month. Peace of mind, whatever the weather. To manage your preferences, visit your account. Policy LM-VH-20831.

units.title: Long Nights are here! Light every corner
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: The nights are long and getting longer, so this week is our Long Nights Lantern Event! Our brightest lanterns ever, with run-time you can trust: the Beacon 900 lasts all night on one charge, guaranteed, or your money back. Why stop at one? Put one at every door, one by every bed and one on the path. Because a dark corner is just a corner you haven't lit yet! The Camp Supply team

units.title: Cold weather
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, with the cold spell forecast for the next few days: - Anti-gel additive is going on the next supply boat for the diesel; please add it as soon as it lands. - Lag the cabin's water feed if you haven't already. - Saw chains are brittle in hard frost, so warm them up before work. - The Met Office says calm and clear, so at least no storm. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Supply drop: manifest
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, draft manifest for the next supply drop: diesel and additive, two-stroke, bar oil, food order as last week plus extra porridge oats (someone asked), gas canisters, first-aid restock, spare filters. Please send any additions by 16:00 tomorrow. The skipper asks that someone is at the dock to meet him by half past two so he can be away again in good time. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a correction to this morning's list: the first-aid restock is coming separately through the safety officer, so it won't be in the main crates. Look for a small grey box with a green label. I've also added hand warmers, which nobody asked for, because I've seen the forecast. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Today's paper
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, you may hear that the Courier ran another piece yesterday about the camp lights being seen from Gilliver. Head office has read it. Nobody is upset with site; it's what a camp looks like at night. The client remains very hands-off and has not asked us anything about it. I'd only ask that nobody on the crew comments online, however tempting. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Payroll flag
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, payroll has flagged the crew wages on the KH-01 account as outstanding again. I know cash on site goes on fuel and kit first, and I know the yard has been slow some days. But the crew's pay has to come first, and head office reads that flag before they read anything else from me. Could you clear it as soon as you're able? Thanks, Ruth

units.title: went to see mum
units.author: sam
units.text: hi, went in to Port Ammet General this afternoon. Mum did six steps with the frame and then told the physio she'd done enough steps for one lifetime. she wants her own nightie and the crossword. the car park machine ate two coins and gave me nothing, so I'm now writing a strongly worded letter in my head. anyway she sends love and says don't do anything daft. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: also the porter who brought her back from x-ray said they've had loads of people in with sprained wrists from falling over in the dark during the power cuts. he said it very cheerfully. I've put a torch by the back door and one by the stairs. you probably have a hundred torches out there. do you? tell me you have torches. x

units.author: sam
units.text: sorry, that was a silly email. I'm tired. the kid asked at tea why you can't just come home at night like normal people and I said because there's no bridge and the boat doesn't go in the dark, and then she asked why the boat doesn't go in the dark and I didn't actually know. it's just a lot of water, I suppose. night x

units.title: the dog has a new trick
units.author: sam
units.text: quick one, the dog has worked out that if he sits by the fridge and sighs loudly enough someone gives him cheese. it's been working on me for a week and I've only just noticed. Mum says he gets it from you. I'm not sure that's a compliment to either of you. anyway the frost is really hard tonight, the car's white already. stay warm. x

units.title: Hot drinks, cold nights
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Quick question: what's in your flask? Whatever it is, keep it hotter for longer with our steel Summit flask, now with a cup that doubles as a lid! Plus: free hand warmer with every Thermal Range order this week. Our warehouse team tested them all on a frosty loading bay so you don't have to. Stay toasty! The Camp Supply team

units.title: Revised accrual: period 3
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Revised accrual statement following the timesheet held during maintenance. Site KH-01, period 3, days 15 to 20 inclusive. Piece rate entries have been reconciled against the yard count submitted by the site lead. Day rate entries have been reconciled against the active roster. No adjustment was required. Reference: KH01-P3-REV1. Queries to Operations only.

units.title: Pay date confirmation
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Pay date notice. Period 3 closes at the end of day 24. Settlement to site account follows on the next banking day. Please ensure the yard count and roster are submitted before period close so that piece and day rates are included. Late submissions roll into period 4. Holiday and sickness codes are not applicable to fixed-term site contracts. Reference: GLS-PD-P3.

units.title: Last chance: Long Nights lanterns
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Our Long Nights Lantern Event ends Sunday! Customers tell us they keep a Beacon 900 burning right through till morning, and honestly, so do we. Order two and get a third at half price. Don't forget spare charge packs: a lantern is only as good as its last hour. See you on the bright side! The Camp Supply team

units.title: Meet the team: we kept the lights on
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: When the power went out across our side of Weyhaven this week, our warehouse team didn't miss a beat! They packed orders by lantern light (ours, of course) and every parcel left on time. A big thank you to Gemma, Raf and the night crew. That's the Camp Supply promise: whatever happens, we deliver. Read their story on our blog.

units.title: Calls about the camp lights
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the office has had three phone calls this week from people in Gilliver about the lights on the Holm. Two were simply curious. One asked whether the crew were all right, which was kind of her. I told all three it's a working camp and lights are normal. Nothing for you to do; I'm just letting you know in case anyone on the supply boat mentions it. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: To be clear, I'm not asking you to change anything about lighting on site. Run the camp however keeps everyone safe and working. I only meant that people across the water can see it, and that some of them are watching more closely than usual because of the papers. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Friday note for head office
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, head office would like a short written note with Friday's numbers this week, rather than just the figure. Three or four lines will do: trees down, yard position, anything holding you up, crew well. I know nobody goes into clearing work for the paperwork. They are reading the papers too, and a calm note from site helps me more than you'd think. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Supply boat timing
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a heads-up: the fuel depot at Gilliver has had trouble with its pump since the first power cut this week and is only filling in the mornings, so the supply boat may be loaded later than planned on its next run. The skipper won't cross late in the day, so if it slips too far he'll go the following morning instead. I'll confirm once I know. Sorry for the faff. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Client contact
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, in case anyone asks, we haven't heard from the client this week, which is entirely normal for them. They set the terms at the start and leave us to it. If someone claiming to be from Ardent Vale contacts the site directly, please let me know before you agree to anything, including a visit. That's standard practice, not a worry. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: A question about the lights
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello, one more question, and then I'll leave you in peace for a while. Several people in Gilliver have told me they watch the camp lights on the Holm each night. Some say the lights stay on until morning. 1. Is that usual for a camp of this kind? 2. Is everyone on site well? I've asked Grieve the same. No name will be used. Best wishes, Nell Ashdown

units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: A short postscript. An older woman in Gilliver asked me to pass on, if I ever reached anyone on the island, that her house keeps a lamp in the window and has done for sixty years. I said I'd try. I don't fully understand it myself, so I'm passing it on exactly as she said it. That's all. Nell

units.title: mum home tomorrow
units.author: sam
units.text: hi, they're letting Mum home tomorrow, which she says is because she's been so charming and the ward says is because they need the bed. I've moved the armchair downstairs and the rug she trips on is in the garage now, which she'll notice and complain about. the kid has drawn her a card with a hip on it. it does not look like a hip. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: anyway I looked at a map tonight. Gilliver to your island is about 9 km. that's nothing, it's less than the drive to Mum's. and it's also loads, because it's water and it's dark. I don't know why I'm telling you that. I suppose I just wanted to see where you are. the paper says the lights are on all night. good. keep them on. x

units.author: sam
units.text: one last thing and then I'll stop clogging your inbox. the dog barked at the back window for twenty minutes tonight. I went out with the torch and it was a hedgehog under the bird table, the size of a fist, not bothered by any of us. I stood in the garden for a bit afterwards. it's so still tonight you can hear the road from the town. x

units.title: Just checking
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, I'm so sorry to bother you. I heard from someone who knows someone at Grieve's office that one of your crew has left the island. Nobody would tell me who. Is Tomas all right? Is he still with you, or is he coming home? If he is with you, please tell him I'm fine and I'm not cross about anything. Thank you. Ana

units.title: A small thing
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, it's Ana again, sorry. Nothing is wrong. I only wanted to say that our mother rang tonight and she's fine too, and the boiler man finally came, so the flat is warm. Tomas always asks about the boiler. Could you tell him? He doesn't sleep well when he's worrying about other people's boilers. Is he sleeping now? Thank you, truly. Ana

units.title: Tell us how we're doing
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Dear Policyholder, we'd love two minutes of your time. How likely are you to recommend Lyle Mutual to a friend or colleague? Your feedback helps us make peace of mind even simpler. Every completed survey this month is entered into a draw for a year's free breakdown cover. This survey closes in fourteen days. You can unsubscribe from feedback requests at any time.

units.title: Roster change acknowledgement
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Automated acknowledgement. The site roster for KH-01 was read at 21:00 Sound Time and matched against the contract headcount. Status: received. No roster change was submitted. If a change was intended, submit it through the site lead form before 21:00 tonight. Changes cannot be backdated. Reference KH01-RST-D18.

units.title: Sound Lines review
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, for completeness: Sound Lines say their night crossing review will run at least until next week. I asked whether that affects crew travel at the end of the contract and was told no, the final pick-up is our own boat in daylight. I'm noting it here so it's in writing. Hope the frost isn't too sharp on site this morning. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: dress rehearsal
units.author: sam
units.text: the dress rehearsal happened. one shepherd cried, one sheep fell off the stage (unhurt, delighted), and ours remembered every line and then said an extra one nobody had written, which got the biggest laugh of the night. the teacher looked like she needed a lie down. I filmed it badly. I'll show you when you're back. x

units.title: Lighting at the dock
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the supply skipper asked me to pass on a request: could the stretch of yard edge where he ties up be kept clear of logs? The light goes early now and he says the approach is gloomy by mid-afternoon. A small thing, but he's the one who brings the porridge. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: sam
units.text: power's back. the fridge made that shuddering noise it makes and the kid cheered. Sound FM said salt on the wires, from the sea. I didn't know salt could do that. apparently it can. the kid's still in the hall in her sleeping bag and I'm not moving her. goodnight. x

units.title: Crew families
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, two crew relatives have rung the office this week asking how everyone is. I've told them the crew are working well and the supply boat runs on schedule, which is true. If any of the crew want a message passed home, send it with Friday's note and I'll make the calls myself. It's no trouble. Thanks, Ruth
